"""scripts/setup_github_action.sh: the Setup section as one idempotent command.

Run against stub `gcloud` and `gh` binaries that record what they were asked
and answer as the real ones would. What is checked is the plan: which
resources are created on a first run, that a second run creates nothing and
converges the provider condition and the role, that an existing environment
is never replaced, that the environment is created protected, that the budget
is the project's and a second repository finds it, that a dry run touches
nothing, and that inputs which could not be safely embedded in a gcloud
argument, a CEL string or a JSON body are refused before anything is called.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import os
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import unittest
from pathlib import Path

_REF_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
SCRIPT = _REF_ROOT / "scripts" / "setup_github_action.sh"
SEP = "\x1f"

_STUB = r'''#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Records every call; answers like the real tool for the reads the script makes.
printf '%s\n' "$(IFS=$'\x1f'; echo "$(basename "$0")$IFS$*")" >> "$STUB_LOG"
if [[ "$1" == "api" && " $* " == *" --input "* ]]; then
  # The body file is gone by the time a test looks; keep its content.
  for ((i=1;i<=$#;i++)); do [[ "${!i}" == "--input" ]] && { j=$((i+1)); cat "${!j}" >> "$STUB_LOG.bodies"; echo >> "$STUB_LOG.bodies"; }; done
fi
case "$(basename "$0") $*" in
  "gcloud auth list"*) echo "someone@example.com" ;;
  "gcloud projects describe"*) echo "123456789" ;;
  "gcloud billing projects describe"*) echo "billingAccounts/ABC-123" ;;
  "gcloud billing budgets list"*) [[ "${STUB_EXISTS:-0}" == 1 ]] && echo "billingAccounts/ABC-123/budgets/b1" ;;
  "gcloud iam workload-identity-pools describe"*"--format=value(state)"*) echo "ACTIVE" ;;
  "gcloud iam roles describe"*) [[ "${STUB_EXISTS:-0}" == 1 ]] || exit 1 ;;
  *" describe "*) [[ "${STUB_EXISTS:-0}" == 1 ]] || exit 1 ;;
  "gh auth status"*) ;;
  "gh api repos/"*"/environments/"*" --jq "*) [[ "${STUB_ENV_EXISTS:-0}" == 1 ]] || exit 1
     case "$*" in *".protection_rules | length"*) echo "${STUB_ENV_RULES:-1}" ;; *protection_rules*) echo "${STUB_ENV_REVIEWERS:-2}" ;; *deployment_branch_policy*) echo "${STUB_ENV_POLICY:-any branch}" ;; esac ;;
  "gh api repos/"*"/environments/"*) [[ " $* " == *" --method "* ]] || { [[ "${STUB_ENV_EXISTS:-0}" == 1 ]] || exit 1; } ;;
  "gh api repos/"*" --jq .id, .owner.id, .full_name"*) printf '4242\n77\n%s\n' "${STUB_CANONICAL:-acme/widgets}" ;;
  "gh api orgs/"*"/teams/"*" --jq .id"*) echo "555" ;;
  "gh api users/"*" --jq .id"*) echo "666" ;;
esac
exit 0
'''


class SetupScriptTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.tmp = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="mantis_setup_gha_"))
        self.addCleanup(shutil.rmtree, self.tmp, ignore_errors=True)
        self.bin = self.tmp / "bin"
        self.bin.mkdir()
        for name in ("gcloud", "gh"):
            p = self.bin / name
            p.write_text(_STUB)
            p.chmod(0o755)
        self.log = self.tmp / "calls.log"

    def run_script(self, *args, exists=False, env_exists=False, **stub_env):
        env = dict(os.environ, PATH=f"{self.bin}:{os.environ.get('PATH', '')}",
                   STUB_LOG=str(self.log), STUB_EXISTS="1" if exists else "0",
                   STUB_ENV_EXISTS="1" if env_exists else "0")
        env.update({k: str(v) for k, v in stub_env.items()})
        proc = subprocess.run(["bash", str(SCRIPT), *args], capture_output=True, text=True,
                              timeout=120, env=env)
        return proc.returncode, proc.stdout + proc.stderr

    def calls(self):
        if not self.log.exists():
            return []
        return [line.split(SEP) for line in self.log.read_text().splitlines()]

    def calls_matching(self, *prefix):
        return [c for c in self.calls() if c[: len(prefix)] == list(prefix)]

    def bodies(self):
        p = Path(str(self.log) + ".bodies")
        return [json.loads(line) for line in p.read_text().splitlines() if line.strip()] if p.exists() else []

    # --- first run ------------------------------------------------------------------

    def test_first_run_creates_everything_pinned_and_protected(self):
        code, out = self.run_script("--project", "my-mantis-scan", "--repo", "acme/widgets",
                                    "--budget-usd", "50", "--github",
                                    "--reviewer-team", "security", "--reviewer-user", "alice")
        self.assertEqual(code, 0, out)
        sa = "mantis-pr-scan@my-mantis-scan.iam.gserviceaccount.com"
        condition = ("assertion.repository_id == '4242' && assertion.repository_owner_id == '77' && "
                     "assertion.repository == 'acme/widgets' && assertion.environment == 'mantis-pr-scan'")
        principal = ("principal://iam.googleapis.com/projects/123456789/locations/global/"
                     "workloadIdentityPools/github/subject/repo:acme/widgets:environment:mantis-pr-scan")
        provider = "projects/123456789/locations/global/workloadIdentityPools/github/providers/mantis"

        enable = self.calls_matching("gcloud", "services", "enable")
        self.assertEqual(len(enable), 1)
        # The least-privilege role, created with exactly the permissions the pipeline needs.
        role = self.calls_matching("gcloud", "iam", "roles", "create", "mantisPrScan")
        self.assertEqual(len(role), 1)
        perms = next(a for a in role[0] if a.startswith("--permissions=")).split("=", 1)[1].split(",")
        self.assertIn("aiplatform.endpoints.predict", perms)
        self.assertIn("monitoring.timeSeries.list", perms)
        self.assertTrue(all(p.startswith(("aiplatform.endpoints.predict", "aiplatform.cachedContents.",
                                          "monitoring.timeSeries.list")) for p in perms), perms)
        self.assertEqual(self.calls_matching("gcloud", "iam", "roles", "update"), [])
        self.assertEqual(len(self.calls_matching("gcloud", "iam", "service-accounts", "create", "mantis-pr-scan")), 1)
        roles = [a for c in self.calls_matching("gcloud", "projects", "add-iam-policy-binding", "my-mantis-scan")
                 for a in c if a.startswith("--role=")]
        self.assertEqual(roles, ["--role=projects/my-mantis-scan/roles/mantisPrScan"],
                         "no predefined create-capable role, no monitoring.viewer")
        self.assertEqual(len(self.calls_matching("gcloud", "iam", "workload-identity-pools", "create", "github")), 1)
        create = self.calls_matching("gcloud", "iam", "workload-identity-pools", "providers", "create-oidc", "mantis")
        self.assertEqual(len(create), 1)
        self.assertIn(f"--attribute-condition={condition}", create[0])
        self.assertIn("--issuer-uri=https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com", create[0])
        # The binding names one subject, not every token the pool maps for the repository.
        bind = self.calls_matching("gcloud", "iam", "service-accounts", "add-iam-policy-binding", sa)
        self.assertEqual(len(bind), 1)
        self.assertIn(f"--member={principal}", bind[0])
        self.assertFalse(any("principalSet://" in a for a in bind[0]))
        # Budget: one per project, named for it, so a second repository finds it.
        budget = self.calls_matching("gcloud", "billing", "budgets", "create")
        self.assertEqual(len(budget), 1)
        self.assertIn("--budget-amount=50USD", budget[0])
        self.assertIn("--display-name=Mantis PR scan (my-mantis-scan)", budget[0])
        # GitHub: the environment is created WITH reviewers, then the three values.
        puts = [c for c in self.calls_matching("gh", "api", "--method", "PUT")
                if c[4] == "repos/acme/widgets/environments/mantis-pr-scan"]
        self.assertEqual(len(puts), 1)
        body = self.bodies()[0]
        self.assertEqual(body["prevent_self_review"], True)
        self.assertEqual(sorted((r["type"], r["id"]) for r in body["reviewers"]),
                         [("Team", 555), ("User", 666)])
        secrets = {c[3]: c[c.index("--body") + 1] for c in self.calls_matching("gh", "secret", "set")}
        self.assertEqual(secrets, {"GCP_WORKLOAD_IDENTITY_PROVIDER": provider,
                                   "GCP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT": sa, "GCP_PROJECT": "my-mantis-scan"})
        for needle in (provider, sa, "GCP_PROJECT", "environment: mantis-pr-scan",
                       "disable-billing-with-notifications", "required reviewers are not optional"):
            self.assertIn(needle, out)
        self.assertNotIn("<project-number>", out)
        self.assertNotIn("WARNING:", out.replace("WARNING: detaching billing", ""))

    def test_the_canonical_repository_name_is_used(self):
        code, out = self.run_script("--project", "my-mantis-scan", "--repo", "ACME/Widgets",
                                    "--no-budget", "--github", "--reviewer-team", "security",
                                    STUB_CANONICAL="acme/widgets")
        self.assertEqual(code, 0, out)
        create = self.calls_matching("gcloud", "iam", "workload-identity-pools", "providers", "create-oidc")
        self.assertTrue(any("assertion.repository == 'acme/widgets'" in a for a in create[0]))
        self.assertIn("canonical name 'acme/widgets'", out)

    # --- second run -----------------------------------------------------------------

    def test_a_second_run_creates_nothing_and_converges(self):
        code, out = self.run_script("--project", "my-mantis-scan", "--repo", "acme/gadgets",
                                    "--repo-id", "9", "--owner-id", "8", "--budget-usd", "75",
                                    exists=True)
        self.assertEqual(code, 0, out)
        creates = [c for c in self.calls() if "create" in c or "create-oidc" in c]
        self.assertEqual(creates, [], creates)
        update = self.calls_matching("gcloud", "iam", "workload-identity-pools", "providers", "update-oidc", "mantis")
        self.assertEqual(len(update), 1)
        self.assertIn("--attribute-condition=assertion.repository_id == '9' && assertion.repository_owner_id == '8' "
                      "&& assertion.repository == 'acme/gadgets' && assertion.environment == 'mantis-pr-scan'",
                      update[0])
        role = self.calls_matching("gcloud", "iam", "roles", "update", "mantisPrScan")
        self.assertEqual(len(role), 1, "the role's permissions converge on this version's list")
        budget = self.calls_matching("gcloud", "billing", "budgets", "update", "billingAccounts/ABC-123/budgets/b1")
        self.assertEqual(len(budget), 1)
        self.assertIn("--budget-amount=75USD", budget[0])
        self.assertNotIn("WARNING:", out.replace("WARNING: detaching billing", ""))

    def test_an_existing_environment_is_never_replaced(self):
        # PUT on an environment resets what it omits -- the reviewers a person
        # added. The script sets the secrets and reports the protection.
        code, out = self.run_script("--project", "my-mantis-scan", "--repo", "acme/widgets",
                                    "--no-budget", "--github", "--reviewer-team", "security",
                                    exists=True, env_exists=True, STUB_ENV_REVIEWERS=2)
        self.assertEqual(code, 0, out)
        self.assertEqual(self.calls_matching("gh", "api", "--method", "PUT"), [])
        self.assertEqual(len(self.calls_matching("gh", "secret", "set")), 3)
        self.assertIn("exists: 2 required reviewer(s)", out)
        self.assertNotIn("WARNING:", out.replace("WARNING: detaching billing", ""))
        # And an existing one with no reviewers is called out, loudly.
        code, out = self.run_script("--project", "my-mantis-scan", "--repo", "acme/widgets",
                                    "--no-budget", "--github", "--reviewer-team", "security",
                                    exists=True, env_exists=True, STUB_ENV_REVIEWERS=0)
        self.assertEqual(code, 0, out)
        self.assertIn("NO required reviewers", out)
        self.assertEqual(self.calls_matching("gh", "api", "--method", "PUT"), [])

    def test_an_environment_github_created_on_its_own_is_configured_as_new(self):
        # A pull request opened before setup makes GitHub create the
        # environment with no protection at all. Nothing a PUT could lose, so
        # the reviewers go on rather than a warning that they are missing.
        code, out = self.run_script("--project", "my-mantis-scan", "--repo", "acme/widgets",
                                    "--no-budget", "--github", "--reviewer-team", "security",
                                    exists=True, env_exists=True, STUB_ENV_REVIEWERS=0, STUB_ENV_RULES=0)
        self.assertEqual(code, 0, out)
        self.assertIn("configured as if new", out)
        self.assertNotIn("NO required reviewers", out)
        puts = [c for c in self.calls_matching("gh", "api", "--method", "PUT")
                if c[4] == "repos/acme/widgets/environments/mantis-pr-scan"]
        self.assertEqual(len(puts), 1)
        self.assertEqual([(r["type"], r["id"]) for r in self.bodies()[0]["reviewers"]], [("Team", 555)])
        # But one with no reviewers and some other rule, or a branch policy,
        # may have been shaped by a person: left alone, as before.
        code, out = self.run_script("--project", "my-mantis-scan", "--repo", "acme/widgets",
                                    "--no-budget", "--github", "--reviewer-team", "security",
                                    exists=True, env_exists=True, STUB_ENV_REVIEWERS=0, STUB_ENV_RULES=0,
                                    STUB_ENV_POLICY="selected branches")
        self.assertEqual(code, 0, out)
        self.assertIn("NO required reviewers", out)
        self.assertEqual(len([c for c in self.calls_matching("gh", "api", "--method", "PUT")]), 1, "no second PUT")

    # --- the refresh side -----------------------------------------------------------

    def test_refresh_mode_pins_main_and_sets_a_branch_rule(self):
        code, out = self.run_script("--project", "my-mantis-scan", "--repo", "acme/widgets",
                                    "--no-budget", "--github", "--refresh")
        self.assertEqual(code, 0, out)
        create = self.calls_matching("gcloud", "iam", "workload-identity-pools", "providers", "create-oidc", "mantis-refresh")
        self.assertEqual(len(create), 1)
        cond = next(a for a in create[0] if a.startswith("--attribute-condition="))
        self.assertIn("assertion.environment == 'mantis-knowledge'", cond)
        self.assertIn("assertion.ref == 'refs/heads/main'", cond)
        bind = self.calls_matching("gcloud", "iam", "service-accounts", "add-iam-policy-binding")
        self.assertTrue(any(a.endswith("/subject/repo:acme/widgets:environment:mantis-knowledge") for a in bind[0]))
        body = self.bodies()[0]
        self.assertEqual(body["deployment_branch_policy"], {"protected_branches": False, "custom_branch_policies": True})
        self.assertNotIn("reviewers", body)
        post = self.calls_matching("gh", "api", "--method", "POST",
                                   "repos/acme/widgets/environments/mantis-knowledge/deployment-branch-policies")
        self.assertEqual(len(post), 1)
        self.assertIn("name=main", post[0])
        self.assertIn("CODEOWNERS", out)
        secrets = [c for c in self.calls_matching("gh", "secret", "set") if c[c.index("--env") + 1] == "mantis-knowledge"]
        self.assertEqual(len(secrets), 3)

    # --- refusals and warnings ------------------------------------------------------

    def test_github_without_reviewers_is_refused_unless_said_out_loud(self):
        code, out = self.run_script("--project", "my-mantis-scan", "--repo", "acme/widgets",
                                    "--no-budget", "--github")
        self.assertEqual(code, 2, out)
        self.assertIn("required reviewers", out)
        self.assertEqual(self.calls(), [])
        code, out = self.run_script("--project", "my-mantis-scan", "--repo", "acme/widgets",
                                    "--no-budget", "--github", "--no-reviewers")
        self.assertEqual(code, 0, out)
        self.assertIn("WARNING", out)
        self.assertIn("NO required reviewers", out)
        body = self.bodies()[0]
        self.assertEqual(body["reviewers"], [])

    def test_a_budget_decision_is_required_on_an_unbudgeted_project(self):
        code, out = self.run_script("--project", "my-mantis-scan", "--repo", "acme/widgets")
        self.assertEqual(code, 2, out)
        self.assertIn("--no-budget", out)
        # Only the reads that answer "does the project have a budget" happened.
        self.assertEqual(sorted({c[1] for c in self.calls()}), ["auth", "billing", "projects"])
        self.assertFalse(any("create" in c for c in self.calls()))
        self.assertEqual(self.calls_matching("gh"), [])

    def test_a_second_repository_on_a_budgeted_project_needs_no_budget_flag(self):
        # The budget is per project. A repository added to a project that has
        # one needs neither flag, and the budget is left as it is.
        code, out = self.run_script("--project", "my-mantis-scan", "--repo", "acme/gadgets",
                                    "--repo-id", "9", "--owner-id", "8", exists=True)
        self.assertEqual(code, 0, out)
        self.assertEqual(self.calls_matching("gcloud", "billing", "budgets", "create"), [])
        self.assertEqual(self.calls_matching("gcloud", "billing", "budgets", "update"), [])
        self.assertIn("existing budget", out)
        self.assertIn("Mantis PR scan (my-mantis-scan)", out)
        self.assertNotIn("No billing budget", out)
        self.assertNotIn("WARNING:", out)

    def test_ids_come_from_gh_without_github_too(self):
        code, out = self.run_script("--project", "my-mantis-scan", "--repo", "acme/widgets", "--no-budget")
        self.assertEqual(code, 0, out)
        create = self.calls_matching("gcloud", "iam", "workload-identity-pools", "providers", "create-oidc")
        cond = next(a for a in create[0] if a.startswith("--attribute-condition="))
        self.assertIn("assertion.repository_id == '4242' && assertion.repository_owner_id == '77'", cond)
        self.assertNotIn("WARNING", out)
        # Nothing on the GitHub side was written: the lookup is the one gh call.
        self.assertEqual([c[:2] for c in self.calls_matching("gh")], [["gh", "auth"], ["gh", "api"]])

    def test_name_only_pinning_warns(self):
        (self.bin / "gh").unlink()
        code, out = self.run_script("--project", "my-mantis-scan", "--repo", "acme/widgets", "--no-budget")
        self.assertEqual(code, 0, out)
        self.assertIn("WARNING", out)
        self.assertIn("by NAME only", out)
        create = self.calls_matching("gcloud", "iam", "workload-identity-pools", "providers", "create-oidc")
        cond = next(a for a in create[0] if a.startswith("--attribute-condition="))
        self.assertNotIn("repository_id", cond)
        # A dry run without gh shows the name-only plan rather than placeholders.
        code, out = self.run_script("--project", "my-mantis-scan", "--repo", "acme/widgets", "--no-budget",
                                    "--dry-run")
        self.assertEqual(code, 0, out)
        self.assertNotIn("<repo-id>", out)
        self.assertIn("by NAME only", out)

    def test_a_role_override_keeps_the_meter_readable(self):
        code, out = self.run_script("--project", "my-mantis-scan", "--repo", "acme/widgets", "--no-budget",
                                    "--repo-id", "1", "--owner-id", "2", "--role", "roles/aiplatform.user")
        self.assertEqual(code, 0, out)
        self.assertEqual(self.calls_matching("gcloud", "iam", "roles"), [])
        roles = sorted(a for c in self.calls_matching("gcloud", "projects", "add-iam-policy-binding")
                       for a in c if a.startswith("--role="))
        self.assertEqual(roles, ["--role=roles/aiplatform.user", "--role=roles/monitoring.viewer"])

    def test_dry_run_calls_nothing_and_shows_the_plan(self):
        code, out = self.run_script("--project", "my-mantis-scan", "--repo", "acme/widgets",
                                    "--environment", "prod-scan", "--budget-usd", "10",
                                    "--github", "--reviewer-team", "security", "--dry-run")
        self.assertEqual(code, 0, out)
        self.assertEqual(self.calls(), [], "a dry run consults nothing")
        self.assertIn("DRY RUN", out)
        self.assertIn("providers create-oidc mantis", out)
        self.assertIn("assertion.environment\\ ==\\ \\'prod-scan\\'", out)
        self.assertIn("gh secret set GCP_PROJECT", out)
        self.assertIn("environment: prod-scan", out)
        self.assertIn("<project-number>", out)
        self.assertIn('"prevent_self_review":true', out)

    def test_inputs_that_cannot_be_embedded_are_refused_before_any_call(self):
        bad = [
            ("--project", "my-mantis-scan", "--no-budget"),                           # no repo
            ("--repo", "acme/widgets", "--no-budget"),                                # no project
            ("--project", "My_Project", "--repo", "acme/widgets", "--no-budget"),
            ("--project", "my-mantis-scan", "--repo", "acme", "--no-budget"),
            ("--project", "my-mantis-scan", "--repo", "acme/widgets'||true", "--no-budget"),
            ("--project", "my-mantis-scan", "--repo", "acme/widgets", "--no-budget", "--environment", "prod scan"),
            ("--project", "my-mantis-scan", "--repo", "acme/widgets", "--no-budget", "--environment", "x' || 'a"),
            ("--project", "my-mantis-scan", "--repo", "acme/widgets", "--budget-usd", "lots"),
            ("--project", "my-mantis-scan", "--repo", "acme/widgets", "--budget-usd", "5", "--no-budget"),
            ("--project", "my-mantis-scan", "--repo", "acme/widgets", "--no-budget", "--pool", "GitHub"),
            ("--project", "my-mantis-scan", "--repo", "acme/widgets", "--no-budget", "--repo-id", "12a"),
            ("--project", "my-mantis-scan", "--repo", "acme/widgets", "--no-budget", "--role", "owner; rm -rf /"),
            ("--project", "my-mantis-scan", "--repo", "acme/widgets", "--no-budget", "--github",
             "--reviewer-team", "sec team"),
            ("--project", "my-mantis-scan", "--repo", "acme/widgets", "--no-budget", "--bogus"),
        ]
        for args in bad:
            code, out = self.run_script(*args)
            self.assertEqual(code, 2, (args, out))
            self.assertIn("error:", out)
            self.assertEqual(self.calls(), [], args)

    def test_help_exits_zero(self):
        code, out = self.run_script("--help")
        self.assertEqual(code, 0, out)
        for flag in ("--budget-usd", "--no-budget", "--reviewer-team", "--refresh", "--repo-id", "--role", "--dry-run"):
            self.assertIn(flag, out)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

"""Regression tests for the October 2026 security review of the reference
harness: each test pins one finding closed, named by its report number.

Nothing here reaches a model or a real sandbox. Where a fix changes what a
model-steered tool may do, the test drives the real tool with the same
arguments the model would send.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
import json
import os
import re
import shutil
import sqlite3
import stat
import sys
import tempfile
import time
import unittest
from pathlib import Path
from unittest import mock

_REF_ROOT = str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent)
if _REF_ROOT not in sys.path:
    sys.path.insert(0, _REF_ROOT)

from core.database import (  # noqa: E402
    init_db, merge_findings, read_findings, update_status, write_findings,
)
from tools.sandbox_tools import check_reached_sink_evidence  # noqa: E402


def _tmpdir(case: unittest.TestCase, prefix: str = "mantis_sec_") -> Path:
    d = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix=prefix)
    case.addCleanup(shutil.rmtree, d, ignore_errors=True)
    return Path(d)


def _finding(title="t", filepath="app.py", severity="HIGH", **kw):
    f = {"title": title, "description": "d", "severity": severity,
         "filepath": filepath, "line_numbers": [1]}
    f.update(kw)
    return f


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# #1 / #6: MCP state lives outside the repository
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


class McpStateOutsideRepoTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        import scripts.mcp_server as mcp_server

        self.mcp = mcp_server
        self.tmp = _tmpdir(self)
        self.repo = self.tmp / "repo"
        self.repo.mkdir()
        (self.repo / "app.py").write_text("def f():\n    return 1\n", encoding="utf-8")
        self.state_root = self.tmp / "state"
        self._env = mock.patch.dict(os.environ, {mcp_server.MCP_STATE_DIR_ENV: str(self.state_root)})
        self._env.start()
        self.addCleanup(self._env.stop)

    def test_default_home_is_outside_the_repository_and_per_repo(self):
        a = self.mcp.MantisState(str(self.repo))
        other = self.tmp / "other"
        other.mkdir()
        b = self.mcp.MantisState(str(other))

            "@@ -5 +6,2 @@\n"
            " five\n"

        # The author of evil.py wrote "++ b/README.md" as its first line; in

        diff = (

class TestScanIndexRestore(unittest.TestCase):
    """A finished scan must leave the shared catalog repo-rooted.

    shared structural index rooted there, so repo-rooted paths stop
    resolving and the gate's blast radius goes blind (found dogfooding:
    callers vanished after the first background scan).

        from core.structural_index import build_structural_index

        tmp = tempfile.mkdtemp()
        self.addCleanup(shutil.rmtree, tmp, ignore_errors=True)

        # its own (narrower) target.
        build_structural_index(str(sub), state.state_dir())
        self.assertFalse(
            state.index().enclosing_symbol("app.py", 2).get("found"))

        # A scan whose subprocess is a no-op: only the restore acts.
        with mock.patch.object(
                mcp_server, "_scan_cmd",
                lambda *a, **k: [sys.executable, "-c", "pass"]):
            out = mcp_server.scan_change(state, ["app.py"])

            deadline = time.time() + 30
            status = {}
            while time.time() < deadline:
                status = mcp_server.scan_status(state, out["scan_id"])
                if status.get("status") in ("done", "finished_with_errors"):
                    break
                time.sleep(0.2)
        self.assertEqual(status.get("status"), "done", status)

"""An empty STOP turn is retried like a 429, and charged like the call it was.

ADK reports a non-streaming turn that finishes with STOP and no parts as
MODEL_RETURNED_NO_CONTENT and the campaign is marked failed over one empty
sample. The model layer now catches that turn before ADK sees it, meters its
usage against the run budget, and sends it back through the same backoff
loop as a rate limit. Past the patience window the empty turn is passed on
unchanged. Streaming is left alone.

class ScriptedUpstream:
    """Stands in for LiteLlm.generate_content_async: one scripted response
    list per call, in order."""

    def __init__(self, calls):
        self.calls = [list(c) for c in calls]
        self.seen = []

    def __call__(self):
        async def generate_content_async(_self, llm_request, stream=False):
            self.seen.append(stream)
            for response in self.calls.pop(0):
                yield response
        return generate_content_async


class EmptyTurnRetryTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.env = mock.patch.dict(os.environ, _FAST)
        self.env.start()
        self.addCleanup(self.env.stop)
        self.llm = ResilientLiteLlm(model="openai/fake")
        self.request = LlmRequest(
            model="openai/fake",
            contents=[types.Content(role="user", parts=[types.Part.from_text(text="look at this")])],
        )

    def with_budget(self, max_tokens=0):
        controller = BudgetController(BudgetConfig(max_tokens=max_tokens), run_id="r")
        token = current_run_context.set(RunContext(jail_dir="", db_path="", budget_controller=controller))
        self.addCleanup(current_run_context.reset, token)
        return controller

    def run_turn(self, upstream, stream=False):
        async def go():
            out = []
            async for r in self.llm.generate_content_async(self.request, stream=stream):
                out.append(r)
            return out

        err = io.StringIO()
        with mock.patch.object(LiteLlm, "generate_content_async", upstream()), contextlib.redirect_stderr(err):
            return asyncio.run(go()), err.getvalue()

    def test_the_condition_is_adk_s(self):
        self.assertTrue(is_empty_stop_response(empty()))
        self.assertTrue(is_empty_stop_response(LlmResponse(finish_reason=types.FinishReason.STOP)))
        self.assertFalse(is_empty_stop_response(good()))
        self.assertFalse(is_empty_stop_response(good(partial=True)))
        blocked = empty()
        blocked.finish_reason = types.FinishReason.SAFETY
        self.assertFalse(is_empty_stop_response(blocked), "a different finish reason is a different problem")
        errored = empty()
        errored.error_code = "SOMETHING"
        self.assertFalse(is_empty_stop_response(errored))
        self.assertTrue(is_retryable_llm_error(MantisEmptyResponseError("x")))

    def test_an_empty_turn_is_retried_and_charged(self):
        controller = self.with_budget()
        upstream = ScriptedUpstream([[empty(1000)], [empty(1000)], [good()]])
        out, err = self.run_turn(upstream)
        self.assertEqual([r.content.parts[0].text for r in out], ["done"])
        self.assertEqual(len(upstream.seen), 3, "two empty turns, one answer")
        self.assertEqual(controller.accumulated_tokens, 2000, "both empty turns were billed, so both are charged")
        self.assertEqual(controller.llm_calls, 2)
        self.assertEqual(err.count("[LLM RETRY]"), 2)
        self.assertIn("returned no content", err)
        self.assertNotIn("passing the empty turn on", err)

    def test_out_of_patience_passes_the_empty_turn_on(self):
        self.with_budget()
        with mock.patch.dict(os.environ, {"MANTIS_LLM_MAX_PATIENCE_SECONDS": "0"}):
            upstream = ScriptedUpstream([[empty()], [good()]])
            out, err = self.run_turn(upstream)
        self.assertEqual(len(upstream.seen), 1, "no patience, no retry")
        self.assertEqual(len(out), 1)
        self.assertTrue(is_empty_stop_response(out[0]), "ADK gets the empty turn and flags it as before")
        self.assertIn("passing the empty turn on", err)

    def test_the_budget_ceiling_stops_the_retries(self):
        controller = self.with_budget(max_tokens=1500)
        upstream = ScriptedUpstream([[empty(1000)], [empty(1000)], [good()]])
        with self.assertRaises(BudgetExceededError):
            self.run_turn(upstream)
        self.assertEqual(len(upstream.seen), 2, "the second empty turn crossed the ceiling")
        self.assertEqual(controller.accumulated_tokens, 2000)

    def test_no_budget_in_context_still_retries(self):
        upstream = ScriptedUpstream([[empty()], [good()]])
        out, _err = self.run_turn(upstream)
        self.assertEqual(len(out), 1)
        self.assertEqual(len(upstream.seen), 2)

    def test_streaming_is_left_alone(self):
        self.with_budget()
        final = LlmResponse(content=types.Content(role="model", parts=[]), finish_reason=types.FinishReason.STOP)
        upstream = ScriptedUpstream([[good("chunk", partial=True), final]])

        self.assertEqual(len(out), 2, "a finish-only chunk after streamed content is normal")
        self.assertEqual(len(upstream.seen), 1)

class _EmptyTurnServer:
    """An OpenAI-compatible endpoint whose every answer is an empty STOP turn
    billed at 1000 tokens. What the bug report's model did, on demand."""

    def __init__(self):
        import threading
        from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, ThreadingHTTPServer

        server = self

        class Handler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
            def log_message(self, *_a):
                pass

            def do_POST(self):
                self.rfile.read(int(self.headers.get("Content-Length", 0)))
                server.requests += 1
                body = json.dumps({
                    "id": "x", "object": "chat.completion", "created": 0, "model": "fake",
                    "choices": [{"index": 0, "message": {"role": "assistant", "content": ""}, "finish_reason": "stop"}],
                    "usage": {"prompt_tokens": 999, "completion_tokens": 1, "total_tokens": 1000},
                }).encode()
                self.send_response(200)
                self.send_header("Content-Type", "application/json")
                self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(body)))
                self.end_headers()
                self.wfile.write(body)

        self.requests = 0
        self.httpd = ThreadingHTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", 0), Handler)
        self.url = f"http://127.0.0.1:{self.httpd.server_address[1]}"
        self.thread = threading.Thread(target=self.httpd.serve_forever, daemon=True)
        self.thread.start()

    def close(self):
        self.httpd.shutdown()
        self.httpd.server_close()


class EndToEndTest(unittest.TestCase):
    """Through ADK, litellm and HTTP: what the pipeline does with a model
    that never says anything."""

    def setUp(self):
        self.server = _EmptyTurnServer()
        self.addCleanup(self.server.close)
        self.tmp = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="mantis_empty_e2e_")
        self.addCleanup(shutil.rmtree, self.tmp, ignore_errors=True)
        self.repo = os.path.realpath(os.path.join(self.tmp, "repo"))
        os.makedirs(self.repo)
        self.target = os.path.join(self.repo, "a.py")
        Path(self.target).write_text("def a():\n    return 1\n")
        self.db = os.path.join(self.tmp, "m.db")

    def run_main(self, patience, *extra):
        env = {k: v for k, v in os.environ.items() if k != "GEMINI_API_KEY"}
        env.update(_FAST)
        env.update({
            "OPENAI_API_KEY": "dummy", "LLM_TIMEOUT": "10",

            "MANTIS_LLM_RETRY_INITIAL_DELAY": "0.2", "MANTIS_LLM_MIN_OFFSET": "0.2", "MANTIS_LLM_RETRY_MAX_DELAY": "0.5",
        })
        proc = subprocess.run(
            [sys.executable, str(_REF_ROOT / "main.py"), self.repo, "--scan-mode", "file-by-file", "--yes",
             "--sandbox", "static-only", "--model", "openai/fake", "--api-base", self.server.url,
             "--max-llm-calls", "30", "--db", self.db, *extra],
            capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=300, env=env, cwd=str(_REF_ROOT))
        return proc.returncode, proc.stdout + proc.stderr

    def ledger(self):
        import sqlite3

        if not os.path.exists(self.db):
            return []
        conn = sqlite3.connect(self.db)
        try:
            return conn.execute("SELECT tokens, llm_calls, metadata_json FROM campaign_spend").fetchall()
        except sqlite3.OperationalError:
            return []
        finally:
            conn.close()

    def test_past_patience_the_campaign_fails_as_before_and_every_turn_is_charged(self):

        self.assertIn("[MantisEmptyResponseError: The model returned no content", out)
        self.assertIn("passing the empty turn on", out)

        self.assertNotIn("BUDGET PAUSE", out)

        tokens, calls, meta = rows[0]
        self.assertEqual(json.loads(meta), {"failed": True}, "the terminal state --resume picks up")

        self.assertEqual((tokens, calls), (1000 * self.server.requests, self.server.requests),
                         "every request the server saw is on the ledger: swallowed turns charged, none twice")

    def test_the_token_budget_pauses_the_run_before_patience_does(self):

        self.assertEqual(code, 2, out[-2000:])
        self.assertIn("BUDGET PAUSE", out)
        self.assertIn("Accumulated tokens 3,000 reached ceiling of 2,500", out)
        self.assertIn("--resume", out)

        self.assertEqual(self.server.requests, 3, "the third empty turn crossed the ceiling; nothing after it")

# Hardened GCE VM Sandbox Setup & Isolation Guide

This guide describes how to provision, harden, and verify a Google Compute
Engine (GCE) VM sandbox for dynamic exploit reproduction and patch verification
in Mantis.

An automated idempotent setup script is provided at
[`reference/scripts/setup_gce_sandbox.sh`](../scripts/setup_gce_sandbox.sh):

```bash
PROJECT_ID="your-project-id" SOURCE_INSTANCE="your-dev-vm" ./reference/scripts/setup_gce_sandbox.sh
```

______________________________________________________________________

## Configuration Variables

Set these environment variables in your shell before running the manual setup
commands:

```bash
export PROJECT_ID="${PROJECT_ID:-$(gcloud config get-value project)}"
export REGION="us-central1"
export ZONE="us-central1-a"
export VPC_NAME="mantis-isolated-vpc"
export SUBNET_NAME="mantis-isolated-subnet"
export SUBNET_RANGE="10.0.0.0/24"
export DNS_POLICY_NAME="mantis-block-public-dns"
export IMAGE_NAME="mantis-assessment-disk-v1"
export DEV_BUILD_VM="my-dev-build-vm"
```

______________________________________________________________________

## 1. Assessment Disk Image Creation & Golden Image Prerequisites

Before capturing your golden assessment disk image from the source build VM,
ensure the following prerequisites are installed and configured:

### Golden Image Prerequisites

1. **Passwordless `sudo` (`NOPASSWD`)**:

   - During instance initialization, `GceEnvironment` provisions the guest
     workspace directory via SSH (`core/environments/gce_env.py:269`):
     ```bash
     sudo mkdir -p /workspace && sudo chown -R $(whoami) /workspace
     ```
   - The SSH user connecting to the sandbox VM must have passwordless `sudo`
     rights in `/etc/sudoers` or `/etc/sudoers.d/` (e.g. standard
     `%sudo ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD:ALL` or `%admin ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD:ALL`).
     Standard GCP Ubuntu LTS images configure this by default for the
     provisioning user.

2. **`python3` Interpreter**:

   - `GceEnvironment` runs automated active in-guest security isolation audits
     (`_verify_guest_isolation()` in `core/environments/gce_env.py:338`) by
     piping a base64-encoded isolation verification script directly to
     `python3`:
     ```bash
     echo '<probe_script>' | base64 -d | python3 -
     ```
   - Ensure `python3` (or `python3-minimal`) is installed on the image and
     available in `PATH` (`/usr/bin/python3`). Without `python3`, instance
     startup fails fail-closed during guest isolation verification.

3. **Pre-Warmed Build Tools & Dependencies**:

   - Because the isolated VPC has zero external internet routing and no Cloud
     NAT, all compilers, build runtimes, package manager caches, test
     frameworks, and dependencies needed to compile the target repository and
     reproduce vulnerabilities must be pre-installed and pre-built on the VM
     before capturing the disk image.

### Image Capture Workflow

1. Provision a development VM with all necessary build runtimes, compilers,
   package managers, and test suites.
2. Confirm that passwordless `sudo` and `python3` are configured as described
   above.
3. Build your target repository on the VM to warm all local build caches,
   dependencies, and artifacts.
4. Capture a custom disk image from the source build VM:

```bash
gcloud compute images create "${IMAGE_NAME}" \
    --project="${PROJECT_ID}" \
    --source-disk="${DEV_BUILD_VM}" \
    --source-disk-zone="${ZONE}" \
    --force \
    --description="Assessment disk image with pre-warmed build dependencies for Mantis"
```

> [!IMPORTANT] **Disk Images vs Machine Images**: Custom disk images
> (`gcloud compute images create --source-disk=...`) allow full instance
> identity override (`--no-service-account --no-scopes`), ensuring the sandbox
> VM runs with zero IAM credentials (`serviceAccounts: null`). GCE Machine
> Images (`--source-machine-image`) lock in the service account identity from
> the source VM and disallow `--no-service-account`.

______________________________________________________________________

## 2. Private Isolated VPC & Network Containment

Create a dedicated VPC with zero external access and Private Google Access
disabled:

```bash
# 1. Custom VPC
gcloud compute networks create "${VPC_NAME}" \
    --project="${PROJECT_ID}" \
    --subnet-mode=custom

# 2. Private subnet (no internet route, no Cloud NAT, no Google API access)
gcloud compute networks subnets create "${SUBNET_NAME}" \
    --project="${PROJECT_ID}" \
    --network="${VPC_NAME}" \
    --region="${REGION}" \
    --range="${SUBNET_RANGE}" \
    --no-enable-private-ip-google-access

# 3. Allow SSH strictly from Google Cloud Identity-Aware Proxy (IAP) IP range
gcloud compute firewall-rules create "allow-iap-ssh-${VPC_NAME}" \
    --project="${PROJECT_ID}" \
    --network="${VPC_NAME}" \
    --allow=tcp:22 \
    --source-ranges=35.235.240.0/20
```

______________________________________________________________________

## 3. Link-Local DNS Exfiltration Defense (`169.254.169.254:53`)

By default in GCE, queries to the link-local metadata resolver
(`169.254.169.254:53`) perform recursive public DNS lookups out-of-band via the
hypervisor, creating an exfiltration path even without external IP routing.

Seal this path at the VPC infrastructure level using Cloud DNS:

### Option A: Cloud DNS Response Policy (RPZ Wildcard Blackhole)

```bash
# Create response policy bound to isolated VPC
gcloud dns response-policies create "${DNS_POLICY_NAME}" \
    --project="${PROJECT_ID}" \
    --networks="${VPC_NAME}" \
    --description="Block all public DNS lookups"

# Wildcard rule returning 0.0.0.0 for all domains (*.)
gcloud dns response-policies rules create block-all-domains \
    --project="${PROJECT_ID}" \
    --response-policy="${DNS_POLICY_NAME}" \
    --dns-name="*." \
    --local-data=name="*.",type="A",ttl=300,rrdatas="0.0.0.0"
```

### Option B: Outbound DNS Server Policy (Private Sinkhole & Logging)

```bash
# Redirect all VM DNS queries away from public recursion to an unassigned private IP
gcloud dns policies create mantis-dns-blackhole \
    --project="${PROJECT_ID}" \
    --networks="${VPC_NAME}" \
    --description="Redirect VM DNS queries to private blackhole" \
    --private-alternative-name-servers=10.0.0.254 \
    --enable-logging
```

______________________________________________________________________

## 4. Mantis Workflow Configuration

Add the GCE sandbox configuration to `workflow.json`:

```json
{
  "sandbox": {
    "type": "gce",
    "options": {
      "project": "YOUR_PROJECT_ID",
      "zone": "us-central1-a",
      "image": "mantis-assessment-disk-v1",
      "subnet": "mantis-isolated-subnet",
      "workdir": "/workspace",
      "tunnel_through_iap": true,
      "no_service_account": true,
      "no_external_ip": true,
      "verify_isolation": true,
      "timeout_seconds": 60
    }
  }
}
```

______________________________________________________________________

## 5. Automated Active Isolation Audit Probes

When `verify_isolation: true` is set (the default), `GceEnvironment` executes an
active in-guest probe before executing any PoCs or analysis tasks:

1. **IAM Token Leak Probe**: Queries
   `http://169.254.169.254/.../service-accounts/default/token`. Fails if access
   tokens are accessible.
2. **Direct Internet Egress Probe**: Attempts TCP connection to external IP
   (`1.1.1.1:80`). Fails if reachable.
3. **Public DNS Recursion Probe**: Attempts resolving `example.com`. Fails if
   public IP is returned.
4. **Private Google Access Probe**: Attempts TCP connection to
   `storage.googleapis.com:443`. Fails if reachable.

If any check fails, the VM is immediately deleted and Mantis halts with a
fail-closed `RuntimeError` detailing the misconfiguration.

______________________________________________________________________

## 6. Single-VM Scope & Multi-VM Architecture Considerations

> [!NOTE] The GCE sandbox setup is currently designed and configured for
> **single-VM execution only**.

If an operator wants to adapt this setup for multi-VM campaigns (e.g.
distributed targets or multi-node exploit chains), they must resolve at least
the following architectural constraints:

1. **DNS Name Resolution (`*.internal`)**: The wildcard Cloud DNS response
   policy (`*.` → `0.0.0.0`) catches everything, including internal metadata
   domains (`*.internal`), making peer VMs unresolvable by hostname. Multi-VM
   setups require explicit private DNS zone rules bypassing the wildcard
   sinkhole for internal peer records.
2. **Internal VM-to-VM Ingress**: The firewall section creates IAP ingress on
   `tcp:22` and nothing else. Because GCP denies ingress by default, all
   VM-to-VM network traffic between sandbox instances is blocked (there is no
   `allow-internal` rule).
3. **Instance Tagging & Firewall Scoping**: Instances created by
   `GceEnvironment` do not currently attach network `--tags`. An operator adding
   an internal communication rule cannot scope it to sandbox VMs by tag, but
   only by CIDR (which means scoping it to the entire subnet).

# Mantis GitHub Action: scan the pull request

`action/` wraps the MCP server's scan tier and deterministic gate (see
[mcp.md](mcp.md)) as a GitHub Action. On every pull request it scans the changed
files with the full Mantis pipeline, runs `check_change` over the PR diff, and
reports the verdict as annotations on the diff plus a step summary.

The action is **advisory and fail-open by default**: the job passes whatever the
verdict, the findings appear as warnings on the changed lines, and a broken
scanner -- a model outage, a setup mistake, a crash -- never stops a merge. Two
inputs change that independently once you trust it on your code: `fail-on` makes
findings fail the job; `fail-closed` makes "Mantis could not look" fail it too.

> **Status: not yet run end-to-end.** Everything below has been tested against
> stubs and read by two security audits, but the action has not yet run against
> a live project: no workflow run, no environment, no credential. Not verified
> by execution: the custom role's permission list against real model calls; the
> hash-pinned install on GitHub's runner image; the daily meter's metric, and
> whether models other than Gemini count in it; metering of the context
> compaction path; how the step summary renders; the knowledge-refresh workflow
> in its entirety; wall time against the 90-minute job timeout on a real diff.
> Until the scan has run cleanly several times, leave `fail-on` and
> `fail-closed` unset, do not set up the refresh workflow (`--refresh`), and on
> the first runs read the scan log for permission denials, the meter line, the
> spend report and the run time. The commit that records those runs should
> remove this note.

## Setup

The scan runs Gemini on the Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform (the service
formerly named Vertex AI; the API, `aiplatform.googleapis.com`, and the
`vertex_ai/` model prefix litellm uses keep their old ids). The job
authenticates with workload identity federation, so the repository holds no
long-lived key. Four things to create: a Google Cloud project that can only run
the model, a spending stop on that project, a GitHub environment that holds the
project's names and gates the job, and the workflow.

### One command

With a project created and billing attached, `scripts/setup_github_action.sh`
does the Google Cloud part, and with `--github` the GitHub part too:

```bash
reference/scripts/setup_github_action.sh --project <project> --repo org/repo \
    --budget-usd <amount> --github --reviewer-team <security-team>
```

It enables the APIs; creates a custom role that can call the model, manage its
context caches and read the project's token meter and nothing else (pass
`--role roles/aiplatform.user` to use the predefined role instead, knowing it
can also create training jobs and endpoints the meter never sees); the service
account with that role; the workload identity pool and a provider whose
condition pins the repository by its numeric id and owner id as well as by name
(read with `gh`, or passed as `--repo-id`/`--owner-id`), from the environment
`mantis-pr-scan` only; and a binding from exactly that subject to the service
account. With `--budget-usd`, a Pub/Sub topic and a billing budget at 50%, 90%
and 100% (`--no-budget` says explicitly that you want none). With `--github`,
the environment -- created **with the required reviewers you name**, self-review
prevented -- and its three secrets. It ends by printing the three values and the
workflow to commit.

Run it again after a failure or a rename and it creates nothing twice: each step
checks first, the provider condition and the role's permissions are updated to
the current ones, and an environment that already exists is never replaced
(replacing it would remove the reviewers a person added), only its secrets set;
its protection is reported, loudly if it has no reviewers. `--dry-run` prints
every command instead. `--environment`, `--service-account`, `--pool` and
`--provider` rename the pieces.

One project can serve several repositories: run the script once per repository
with its own `--provider` and `--service-account`. The pool, the role and the
budget are shared -- the budget caps the project, not a repository, so the
second run finds it and needs neither budget flag. So is the daily token meter
(see Spend). No repository gets a grant on the project itself; each one's
identity can act only as its own service account.

For the knowledge-refresh workflow, run it a second time with `--refresh`: a
second provider admitting `refs/heads/main` from the `mantis-knowledge`
environment only, and that environment created with a deployment-branch rule of
`main`.

Two things it leaves to you, and says so: the function that detaches billing
when the budget is spent (The spending stop, below), and the reading the
reviewers do before approving a run. The sections that follow are what the
script does, for doing it by hand or for checking its work.

### Google Cloud

One project reserved for this, with billing attached. Replace `org/repo` with
your repository and keep the environment name if you keep it in the workflow.

```bash
PROJECT=<project>
gcloud config set project "$PROJECT"
NUMBER=$(gcloud projects describe "$PROJECT" --format='value(projectNumber)')

# The model API, the project's own usage meter, and what workload identity
# needs to mint and exchange tokens.
gcloud services enable aiplatform.googleapis.com monitoring.googleapis.com \
    iamcredentials.googleapis.com iam.googleapis.com sts.googleapis.com

# A role that can call the model, manage its context caches, and read the
# project's meter -- and nothing else. roles/aiplatform.user would also let
# the token create training jobs and endpoints the meter never sees.
gcloud iam roles create mantisPrScan --project="$PROJECT" --title="Mantis PR scan" \
    --permissions=aiplatform.endpoints.predict,aiplatform.cachedContents.create,aiplatform.cachedContents.get,aiplatform.cachedContents.list,aiplatform.cachedContents.update,aiplatform.cachedContents.delete,monitoring.timeSeries.list

# A service account with that role.
gcloud iam service-accounts create mantis-pr-scan --display-name="Mantis PR scan"
SA="mantis-pr-scan@$PROJECT.iam.gserviceaccount.com"
gcloud projects add-iam-policy-binding "$PROJECT" \
    --member="serviceAccount:$SA" --role="projects/$PROJECT/roles/mantisPrScan"

# A pool with a GitHub OIDC provider, admitting one repository -- by its
# numeric ids, which a renamed or re-created repository cannot reuse, and by
# name -- from one environment. gh api repos/org/repo --jq '.id, .owner.id'
# gives the ids.
gcloud iam workload-identity-pools create github --location=global \
    --display-name="GitHub Actions (Mantis)"
gcloud iam workload-identity-pools providers create-oidc mantis \
    --location=global --workload-identity-pool=github \
    --issuer-uri="https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com" \
    --attribute-mapping="google.subject=assertion.sub,attribute.repository=assertion.repository" \
    --attribute-condition="assertion.repository_id == '<repo-id>' && assertion.repository_owner_id == '<owner-id>' && assertion.repository == 'org/repo' && assertion.environment == 'mantis-pr-scan'"

# Let exactly that repository's jobs in that environment impersonate the
# service account: one subject, not every token the pool maps for the repo.
gcloud iam service-accounts add-iam-policy-binding "$SA" \
    --role="roles/iam.workloadIdentityUser" \
    --member="principal://iam.googleapis.com/projects/$NUMBER/locations/global/workloadIdentityPools/github/subject/repo:org/repo:environment:mantis-pr-scan"

# The three values GitHub needs.
gcloud iam workload-identity-pools providers describe mantis \
    --location=global --workload-identity-pool=github --format='value(name)'
echo "$SA"
echo "$PROJECT"
```

### The spending stop

The action bounds what one run spends (see Spend). What the project may spend in
a month is yours to decide and yours to enforce, because the platform will not
do it for you: Gemini on the Agent Platform draws on dynamic shared quota, which
has no per-project ceiling to lower, and a budget on its own only sends mail.
Wire the budget to something that cuts the project off:

```bash
BILLING=$(gcloud billing projects describe "$PROJECT" --format='value(billingAccountName)')
gcloud pubsub topics create mantis-pr-scan-budget
gcloud billing budgets create --billing-account="${BILLING#billingAccounts/}" \
    --display-name="Mantis PR scan" --budget-amount=<amount>USD \
    --filter-projects="projects/$NUMBER" \
    --threshold-rule=percent=0.5 --threshold-rule=percent=0.9 \
    --threshold-rule=percent=1.0 \
    --notifications-rule-pubsub-topic="projects/$PROJECT/topics/mantis-pr-scan-budget"
```

Then, if you want the stop to be automatic, subscribe a function to the topic
that detaches billing from the project when the message's `costAmount` reaches
`budgetAmount`. Google publishes the function and the IAM it needs:
[Disable billing with notifications](https://docs.cloud.google.com/billing/docs/how-to/disable-billing-with-notifications);
deploy it as written.

> **Warning.** Detaching billing shuts down every billable service in the
> project, and Google's own page warns that resources in it can be stopped and
> their data lost. That is the point here, and it is safe only in a project that
> holds nothing you would miss: this service account, this pool, this budget,
> and nothing else. Never attach this stop to a project with persistent
> resources, data, or anything another system depends on. Re-attaching billing
> afterwards is a manual step, and until someone does it every scan fails with a
> setup error, which is the behaviour you want from a stop.

Pick `<amount>` as the most you are prepared to lose to a bug in a month, not as
a forecast. Budget data lags by hours; the stop is for a runaway that lasts a
day, and the action's own limits are for the one that lasts a run.

### GitHub

1. Create an environment named `mantis-pr-scan` (Settings, Environments) and
   **put required reviewers on it**. This is not optional. On a `pull_request`
   event GitHub runs the pull request's own copy of the workflow file, and a job
   that declares the environment receives its secrets and can mint the identity
   token the provider accepts. Without reviewers, anyone who can push a branch
   can edit the workflow to send the credential wherever they like, remove every
   budget, or run anything at all with it, and the run happens before anyone
   reads the pull request. Branch protection and CODEOWNERS gate the merge, not
   the run; a deployment-branch rule does not help either, because the run's ref
   is the merge ref. The reviewers are the control: a person approves each run,
   and before approving reads the diff of `.github/workflows/mantis-pr-scan.yml`
   (and, if you run the action from this repository with `uses: ./action`, of
   `action/` and `reference/`). Turn on "prevent self-review"; leave
   administrator bypass off unless the administrators are the reviewers. The
   provider condition above admits tokens from this environment only, so the job
   must declare it.

2. On that environment, add three secrets: `GCP_WORKLOAD_IDENTITY_PROVIDER` (the
   provider's full resource name,
   `projects/<number>/locations/global/workloadIdentityPools/github/providers/mantis`),
   `GCP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT`, and `GCP_PROJECT`. None of them is a credential;
   keeping them out of the workflow file keeps your project ids out of the
   public record and out of the job log.

3. If the organisation allows only selected actions, allow
   `google-github-actions/auth@*`; the others are under `actions/`.

4. Add the workflow. Pin every action to a full commit SHA. This repository's
   own `.github/workflows/mantis-pr-scan.yml` is this file with
   `uses: ./action`.

   ```yaml
   name: Mantis PR scan
   on:
     pull_request:
       types: [opened, synchronize, reopened, ready_for_review]
     workflow_dispatch:
       inputs:
         base-sha:
           description: Commit to diff the checked-out ref against.
           required: true
   permissions:
     contents: read
     id-token: write
   concurrency:
     group: mantis-pr-scan-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.run_id }}
     cancel-in-progress: true
   jobs:
     scan:
       if: >-
         github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' ||
         (github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository &&
          !github.event.pull_request.draft &&
          github.event.pull_request.user.type != 'Bot')
       runs-on: ubuntu-latest
       timeout-minutes: 90
       environment: mantis-pr-scan
       steps:
         - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
           with:
             fetch-depth: 0
             persist-credentials: false
         - uses: google-github-actions/auth@7c6bc770dae815cd3e89ee6cdf493a5fab2cc093 # v3.0.0
           with:
             workload_identity_provider: ${{ secrets.GCP_WORKLOAD_IDENTITY_PROVIDER }}
             service_account: ${{ secrets.GCP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT }}
         - uses: google/mantis/action@<commit-sha>
           env:
             GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT: ${{ secrets.GCP_PROJECT }}
           with:
             model: vertex_ai/gemini-3.8-flash
             base-sha: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha || inputs.base-sha }}
   ```

   `id-token: write` lets the job mint the OIDC token the auth step exchanges
   and grants nothing else. `fetch-depth: 0` makes the base commit available for
   the diff; without it the action fetches that one commit on its own, which
   works on public repositories and on private ones as long as the checkout kept
   its credentials. The `if` skips drafts until they are marked ready and skips
   bot-authored pull requests; both are runs nobody reads (see Spend).

### Repository settings

Settings only a repository administrator can make, and the action's design
assumes them, in any repository that installs it:

- **Rulesets on `main`**: require a pull request with at least one approval,
  require status checks, block force pushes, restrict deletions, and keep the
  bypass list to break-glass actors.
- **CODEOWNERS** naming a security owner for `.github/workflows/`, `action/`
  (when dogfooding), and `.mantis/knowledge/`, with "require review from code
  owners" on. The workflow file is what a pull request can rewrite; the
  knowledge directory is what later scans believe.
- **Actions permissions**: default `GITHUB_TOKEN` permissions set to read, and
  "Allow GitHub Actions to create and approve pull requests" left **off**. The
  refresh workflow copes: it pushes its branch and prints the link to open the
  pull request by hand when it may not open one itself.
- **Allowed actions**: if the organisation restricts actions, allow
  `google/mantis/action@*` and `google-github-actions/auth@*`; everything else
  this uses is under `actions/`, `github/` or `ossf/scorecard-action` and is
  pinned to a commit.
- **Dependabot** alerts and security updates on; secret scanning on. Version
  updates (the scheduled pin bumps) are a separate choice: a
  `.github/dependabot.yml` with a cooldown, or whatever else keeps your pins
  moving.
- **Scheduled workflows stop after 60 days without repository activity**, the
  refresh included; a repository that idles needs a push, or a manual dispatch,
  to wake it.

If the project the action authenticates to is inside Google's own cloud
organisation, note that workload identity federation from GitHub is denied by
policy there and needs an exception before the provider can be created; a
project outside that organisation does not. External users of this action are
not affected.

### First run

Run the workflow by hand (Actions, Mantis PR scan, Run workflow) with `base-sha`
set to any ancestor of the branch, approve it if the environment asks, and read
the result:

- The auth step fails: the provider condition does not match (the `environment`
  claim is in the token only because the job declares `environment:`; the name
  must be the same in both places), the service account binding carries the
  wrong project number, or `iamcredentials.googleapis.com` is not enabled. The
  step's error says which.
- The action exits 3 with a setup error: the preflight found no project, the
  platform rejected the credential, or the project's token meter could not be
  read for the daily budget (the service account needs
  `roles/monitoring.viewer`). The summary names what is missing. A rejected
  credential is reported this way, once, rather than as a failed scan on every
  file.
- A verdict and a summary: done. Pull requests from branches of the repository
  now trigger it on their own; forks are skipped by the `if`.

Set `VERTEXAI_LOCATION` on the step if the model is not served from `global`.
Other pipeline knobs are plain environment variables there too: `LLM_TIMEOUT`
(seconds per model call), `REASONING_EFFORT` (`low`, `medium`, `high`), and
`LLM_MAX_TOKENS`.

The `model` input takes any id the pipeline (litellm) accepts, with that
provider's credentials in `env:` on the step; the preflight asks each provider
for its own requirements. Recall differs by model and endpoint, and the verdict
reports what the model found, only that. This document covers the Agent Platform
route alone.

## Spend

The job holds a model credential while reading attacker-influenced input, on a
platform whose quota for Gemini is dynamic and shared: there is no per-project
ceiling to lower. Whatever bounds the bill therefore has to be in the action
itself, in the unit the invoice uses, and the only thing left to the platform is
the stop of last resort. Two failure modes, two different limits: one pull
request engineered to burn money, and a day on which runs do not stop coming.

### One budget per run

`max-tokens` is the hard limit on what one run can spend. The driver, not the
model, does the arithmetic:

- Every token counts at full price, whether or not the provider served it from
  cache, so the number bounds the worst case the invoice can show rather than
  the expected one.
- The budget is shared out as the run goes: each file is launched with an equal
  share of what is still unspent, so a cheap file's unspent share passes to the
  files after it and one expensive file cannot take the whole run. Each scan is
  told its share as its own ceiling and pauses when it reaches it.
- Each scan reports what it spent; a scan that reports nothing, because it was
  killed or crashed first, is charged its whole share. The budget can
  over-count, never under-count.
- A file whose share has fallen below 100,000 tokens is not launched (the
  smallest scan costs about 250,000; see Sizing). It is reported unscanned,
  which floors the verdict at REVIEW with the file named, exactly as a timeout
  would. Nothing in the pull request can raise the budget.

The step summary prints the figure for every run: tokens per file, the run total
against the budget, and the files the budget did not reach. The JSON report
carries the same under `usage` and per file under `scan.results`.

The budget is checked after each model response, so a scan can overshoot its
share by at most one request. The next layer bounds that request.

### One ceiling per request

`max-input-tokens` caps the input of any single model request. The pipeline
refuses a larger request before dispatch, whatever the model's context window
and even for a model litellm cannot look up (an `api-base` gateway, say), where
the window-relative guard would otherwise not apply. A request the cap refuses
fails that file's scan, which is REVIEW with the file named. With the cap, the
most one run can spend is `max-tokens` plus one request of `max-input-tokens`
per file, and the most one request can cost is known before the model is chosen.

### One budget per day

The two numbers above bound a run; `daily-token-budget` bounds the day, and it
does so from the platform's own meter rather than from anything this code
remembers, because the action keeps no state between runs and should not. Before
scanning, the driver reads from Cloud Monitoring how many tokens the project was
served in the trailing 24 hours (every model, input and output, the figure the
invoice is built from) and sets this run's budget to the smaller of `max-tokens`
and what is left of the day. Nothing left: nothing is launched, every file is
reported unscanned, and the verdict is REVIEW naming the day's figure. Something
left: the run proceeds with the smaller budget and the summary says so.

The meter is per project, so every repository that authenticates to the project
shares the one budget, which is the point. The meter runs a few minutes behind,
and concurrent runs each read it at their own start, so the day's figure can be
overshot by about one run budget per run in flight plus those minutes; the
billing stop below is the backstop behind that.

A daily budget that is set but cannot be read (the role is missing, the API is
off, the route has no Google Cloud project) is a setup error, exit 3, with the
fix named: a limit that is silently skipped is not a limit. `0` turns the check
off explicitly, which is the setting for a route other than the Agent Platform.

### Fewer runs

Nothing bounds how many runs a day there are except what triggers them; the
daily budget catches the day when that goes wrong, and these make it less
likely. The workflow above trims the runs nobody reads: drafts wait until they
are marked ready, bot-authored pull requests (dependency bumps) are skipped, and
`concurrency` with `cancel-in-progress` keeps a force-push from stacking runs on
one pull request. Same-repository pull requests only means every remaining run
was started by someone with push access.

If you need a ceiling on runs in flight across the repository, add a job-level
`concurrency` group without `cancel-in-progress`; runs then queue one at a time.
GitHub keeps only one queued run per group and cancels the rest, so a burst of
pull requests leaves some with a cancelled check until their next push. Fine for
an advisory check; think twice before combining it with `fail-on`.

### The stop of last resort

Everything above is this code; if it has a bug, nothing on the platform side
stops spend on its own. The one deterministic stop the platform offers is a
billing budget wired to an action that cuts the project off, set up under The
spending stop above. It is yours to do: Mantis bounds what one run spends and
what one day spends; what the project may lose to a bug in a month is a decision
only its owner can make.

### Sizing

Measured with a Gemini model, calls uncapped in practice, every token at full
price:

| File        | Tokens | Calls | Minutes |
| ----------- | ------ | ----- | ------- |
| 20 lines    | 261k   | 44    | 7       |
| 440 lines   | 353k   | 45    | 19      |
| 1,000 lines | 658k   | 51    | 14      |
| 2,000 lines | 853k   | 60    | 13      |

Calls stay well under the cap; tokens are what grows with the file, which is why
tokens are the unit. The floor is about 250k whatever the file (prompts and
graph nodes), and size adds roughly 300k per thousand lines. The defaults follow
from the table:

- `max-tokens: 10M`: a pull request of ten ordinary files finishes whole (1M a
  file); a twenty-five-file one gets 400k a file, enough for files up to a few
  hundred lines, and its biggest pause at their share with the verdict saying
  which. Below 100k a share is not worth launching and the file is reported
  unscanned instead.
- `daily-token-budget: 100M`: forty typical runs, or ten at the worst case, in
  any 24 hours. A repository that sees more pushes than that in a day raises it
  knowingly; a trigger that fires every minute is stopped within hours.
- `max-input-tokens: 262144`: a quarter of the smallest Gemini window and
  several times the largest request an ordinary scan makes.

Read your own summaries for a week before changing any of them. A budget that is
too small shows up as REVIEW with files named, never as a silent pass. Minutes
per file set the other limit: the job's `timeout-minutes` ends a run that is
still scanning, and the files it did not reach are REVIEW too.

#### In money

The budgets are in tokens because tokens are what the action can count. What
they cost is your model's price on the day, which this document does not quote:
multiply the rows below by the per-token price of the model you configure, with
output taken as about an eighth of the tokens and no prompt caching. The
defaults were sized for the default model.

| Budget                                | Tokens |
| ------------------------------------- | ------ |
| One ordinary file                     | 500k   |
| One pull request, 4 files             | 2M     |
| `max-tokens: 10M`, worst case per run | 10M    |
| `daily-token-budget: 100M`, per day   | 100M   |
| … for a month nobody looked           | 3,000M |

The last row is the one to size for. Decide what a month of unnoticed abuse may
cost you, divide by your model's blended price per token to get the month in
tokens, divide by thirty for `daily-token-budget`, and set the billing stop
(Setup) just above that month. A model that costs several times more per token
than the default needs budgets several times smaller for the same ceiling -- on
the order of `max-tokens: 3M` and `daily-token-budget: 30M` at a tenfold price
difference. The defaults are chosen so that ordinary pull requests finish whole
and a day of abuse is bounded, not so that nothing can ever be wasted: a run
that pauses short of finishing has spent the tokens and produced less, which is
the more expensive failure.
